newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fernandez vows firm hand against Argentine lobbies.
newsitem.headline: Fernandez vows firm hand against Argentine lobbies.

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, stung by criticisms from his predecessor Domingo Cavallo, promised Thursday a firm hand against lobby and pressure groups to keep economic policy on course.
"These lobbies and pressure groups are real and can have a harmful impact on public finances and the well-being of the Argentine people," Fernandez told a business conference.
"But they must be fought with a firm and realistic stance, and always using the institutions of democracy."

Fernandez made a veiled attack on Cavallo, who has called him "either dishonest or incapable" for endorsing a businessman Cavallo accuses of graft. Cavallo has also accused him of "weakness," which "shows itself in higher public spending..."
Without mentioning Cavallo by name, Fernandez hit back at his predecessor for saddling him with a $6.0 billion budget deficit this year -- twice the size expected.
"Argentina is growing up. It's no use hiding the deficit with false optimism and trying to deceive parliament and analysts with unrealistic forecasts," said the minister.
Cavallo was sacked in July after doing a widely-praised job in reducing Argentina's hyperinflation to zero, fostering growth and pegging the peso to the dollar.
The former minister is now on a noisy crusade against corruption which has pitted him against Supreme Court judges and senior members of President Carlos Menem's cabinet.
Fernandez, whose quiet demeanor contrasts markedly with Cavallo's confrontational saber-rattling, warned against "omnipotence" and said: "We should talk less and do more."

But the minister believes this "mature" new Argentina can ride out Cavallo's legal battles with the economy intact: "The reforms are solid enough for the economy not to depend on people, but on institutions."
